title: Hyp Cantor Core
objective: Implement prepared packed source-transparent genus-2/3 public Cantor arithmetic and batched scalar operations with the ordinary reference fallback.

handoff.summary: Implements ordinary-Python, source-transparent prepared Cantor arithmetic for odd-degree one-infinity genus-2/3 Jacobians over supported odd prime fields. The public context provides exact canonical row packing/fingerprints, dynamic/native add, double, scalar, negate, subtract, sum, progression and fused BSGS batches, exact fallback/status diagnostics, resource limits, lazy Kummer composition, and opaque owner-bound packed batches. Native read-only consumers borrow authenticated capsule storage without copying; dynamic/public consumers get explicit owned copies. Lazy divisors are owner-registered before escape, while already-materialized divisors always derive and validate their row from `(u,v)`, closing capsule transplant, owner-rebound, and split-brain attacks. Finite-field divisor pickle state serializes only validated mathematical model and `(u,v)` data, never opaque storage. Exhaustive small-field, collision/general-h, current-kernel, CPython, compiled, scalar, fused-search, mutation-isolation, serialization, and public Jacobian differentials pass, together with the retained QQ smoke on the required integration base. The final local p=1009 1,000-item receipt is 2.954/3.762ms retained add, 9.275/8.504ms registered ordinary-public add, 0.678/0.963s retained 256-bit scalar, and 0.222/0.237s after forced add materialization for genus 2/3. Authenticated gathering prepares 1,000 already-registered public divisors in 1.624/1.500ms and cached prepared batches in 0.026/0.021ms. The raw addon is 1.049x/1.047x the exact same-source standalone genus-2/3 core under production bounds/link flags and matched 10-warmup plus 9-by-50-call samples, closing the 1.15x boundary gate with identical digests.
risks: The exact v1 domain is deliberately limited to odd-degree one-infinity models, odd prime fields, genus 2/3, and p <= 2^32-1. Even-degree divisors need a versioned weight/infinity coordinate and an additional v slot and are rejected rather than misencoded.

The plan's truly fresh pack/unpack criterion remains open. Preparing 1,000 distinct, unregistered, checked public divisors costs 0.823/0.876s because the boundary conservatively repeats the Mumford relation validation; constructing and preparing them costs 2.461/2.610s. Eager per-owner constructor capsules shifted the same work into construction, regressed constructor-only timing by about 21%, and did not materially improve the paired total, so that misleading optimization was reverted. Registered kernel/public results and explicit retained batches are separate faster contracts and are not relabeled as fresh input.

Same-host Magma 1,000-element 256-bit scalar parity, quiet bench-1 acceptance, Windows x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64 receipts remain integration work; no competitiveness claim is made from the noisy local host alone.
Forced publication of 1,000 polynomial `(u,v)` objects still costs about 0.22-0.24s and dominates materialized batches; the opaque retained contract deliberately avoids that cost until demanded.

The recorded broad `pnpm test:native` run passed its production build, native integration, FFLAS, graph, M4RI, FFI, sanitizer, production-kernel, and matrix stages, then failed at the final out-of-claim `test/dense-rational-migration.cjs:321` expectation: the compiler now reports the source-correct `integer-buffer-values` backend where the stale ratchet expects `tagged`. Integration accepted this shared compiler-test mismatch for correction and final rerun on the merged root.
next_steps: Integrate the compiler prerequisite commits first, then the complete implementation and benchmark receipt from this branch, retaining the production registrations and strict/native package split maintained by integration.

Design a lightweight authenticated validated-construction provenance only if it improves the exact combined construction-plus-first-prepare contract without slowing constructor-only or internal `check=False` paths; the rejected eager-capsule experiment is the baseline.

Run quiet same-contract Magma and Sage.js add/scalar receipts on bench-1 only after authorization, then validate the exact digest and dynamic fallback across Windows x64, Linux arm64, and macOS arm64.

Keep legacy in-core FLINT BSGS first for genus-3 certification until the fused source-transparent progression wins an end-to-end consumer benchmark; the exact fused kernel remains a fallback/challenger.
Verify and update the shared dense-rational backend-explain ratchet on the merged compiler root, then rerun `pnpm test:native`; no finite Cantor failure occurred in the recorded broad run.
